item.title: The U.S. last held a public execution in the 1930s. The Pentagon wants to change that
item.description: The Pentagon says it will livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan at Fort Hood, the site of his 2009 mass shooting. That would be the first public execution in the U.S. since the 1930s.
item.content:encoded:
The Pentagon says it will livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan at Fort Hood, the site of his 2009 mass shooting. That would be the first public execution in the U.S. since the 1930s.

(Image credit: Getty Images)

item.title: Did Russia play by the rules in reporting lab worker's death?

item.title: Why American investors love European defense startups
item.description: As European defense spending takes off, just about half of the funding in Europe's defense tech industry is coming from American investors this year. One reason why: European investment firms have restrictions on how they can invest.

item.title: ChatGPT for Teens has special safeguards. A watchdog group finds most don't work
item.description: A study from Common Sense Media says most safeguards in ChatGPT for Teens failed. The chatbot talks to teens like a friend and doesn't alert parents when users talk about self-harm and suicide.

item.title: Why mailing a ballot close to Election Day may get it rejected for a late postmark
item.description: If you're using the U.S. Postal Service to return a ballot close to Election Day, officials recommend getting it postmarked at a post office to avoid getting caught up in mail processing changes.

item.title: In Central African Republic, deported immigrants find themselves in limbo
item.description: The Trump administration says it has deported more than 25,000 people to countries to which they have no ties. NPR spoke to three men who say it feels like they've lost control over their own lives.
